description: Goggles. Three stars draw a pair of goggles, shown for two full laps.
name: Goggles orbit

description: Yin yang Ia. Three stars trace a yin yang pattern, shown for two full laps. Their close passes need very small time steps.
name: Yin yang orbit

description: Moth I. Three stars repeat a dance shaped like a moth, shown for two full laps.
name: Moth I orbit

description: Two disk galaxies swing past each other, with the work split across four workers. The result matches one worker doing it all down to the last digits. The collision is chaotic, so those tiny differences grow late in the run.
name: Galaxy collision on four workers

description: Two disk galaxies swing past each other, with the forces from a faster tree method that approximates them. The overall shape is right, but single stars end up slightly off from where exact forces would put them.
name: Galaxy collision with a tree method

description: Two disk galaxies swing past each other. Gravity pulls out a bridge of stars and then two long tails. One worker computes the exact forces.
name: Galaxy collision with exact forces

description: Three stars on a figure eight orbit, moved with RK4. It is very accurate, but it computes the forces four times per step.
name: Figure eight with RK4

description: Three stars on a figure eight orbit, moved with Simple Euler, the most basic method. The stars slowly drift off the figure eight and the energy keeps growing.
name: Figure eight with Simple Euler

description: Three stars chase each other around a figure eight. Velocity Verlet keeps the loop closed and the energy steady.
name: Figure eight with Velocity Verlet
